observation: Experienced foragers performed better with substrate trails than either information source alone.
mechanism: Personal route recall combined with locally detected substrate marks; confidence is an interpretation.
confidence: High for experimental effect; low for our exact navigation representation
methods: Marked individual foragers; 21 cm walkway with replaceable 7 cm paper section; one or three prior visits; video analysis.
measurements: Article abstract: walking speed +25%, straightness +30% with combined information. Results use contrast-specific estimates; these are not universal coefficients.
validation: C and C-controlled; playback and hidden-resource tests
simplification: Perfect loop-erased odometry and exact remembered cells, no visual landmarks; 1.25 speed multiplier encodes the effect rather than independently predicting it.

observation: Food exchange networks are spatial and heterogeneous.
mechanism: Encounter-mediated donor/receiver crop transfers; exact flow rates were not measured in this paper.
confidence: High for contact exchange; low for mass-flow calibration
methods: Five queenless, broodless worker groups, at least 50 each; four-day deprivation; 3 mL 1 M sucrose; 90 min video including 30 min baseline; minute scans.
measurements: Mandible contact >5 s defined an event; group size 53.4 ± 5.2 workers; 99.0 ± 17.4 interactions. Duration/event counts are proxies, not µg measurements.
simplification: Same-cell contact, 6 s wait, difference-driven transfer; protein pool treats soluble processed nutrients as crop-compatible. No anatomical digestion model.

observation: Limited feeding access changes collective allocation and permits flexibility.
mechanism: Reduced intake and recruitment when workers compete locally for food.
methods: Six queenless colonies, 2400–4700 workers; 1 M feeders with 1/3/9/27 holes; delayed second feeder at 15 min.
measurements: Stable trials 120 min; changing trials 90 min. Published ABM uses 60 s drinking and unloading, but explicitly is not fully parameterized L. niger biology.
implementation: Simulation.updateWorker: intake and successful recruitment divided by local occupancy
validation: B; feeding contact and conservation tests
simplification: No explicit feeder holes or queue; crowding factor 1/(1+n) is unfitted.

observation: Workers collectively assemble pillars and caps; natural CT nests have galleries/chambers.
mechanism: Material-associated marks and local geometry explain laboratory deposition patterns, not necessarily subterranean excavation.
confidence: High for published deposition experiments; low for our underground rule
methods: Groups of 500 workers building on 3 mm moist sand/clay substrate; CT imaging of two natural nests.
measurements: Natural nest chamber/gallery height peaks 5.9 and 5.5 mm; widths centred near 12 mm; two nests are not a population distribution.
implementation: World.dig and Simulation.updateWorker replace plan with local work; soil transported to surface
validation: G, soil conservation; qualitative geometry diagnostics only
simplification: 2D cell removal, provisional work threshold; no claimed replication of topochemical mound construction or structural mechanics.

observation: Queens can actively form founding associations; mature colonies generally retain one queen.
mechanism: Queen association is context-dependent, followed by conflict after worker emergence.
confidence: High for species organization; single-queen scenario intentionally narrower
methods: Laboratory settling choices among nest chambers with newly mated queens.
measurements: Introduction reports 18–25% cofounding in groups of 2–5 in cited field studies; not a parameter fitted here.
implementation: One mated queen; separate founding and established initial conditions
simplification: No cofoundress conflict, mating flight, sperm dynamics or reproductive castes.

observation: Temperature and natal elevation alter nest depth/complexity.
confidence: Species boundary established; no L. niger parameter inferred
methods: Factorial high/low natal elevation and excavation temperature study; publisher abstract available; full-text retrieval later blocked.
implementation: Not used to calibrate L. niger; temperature model explicitly provisional
simplification: Excluded as species-mismatched evidence for precise rules.

observation: Local interactions and environmental context shape collective dynamics.
mechanism: Encounter-based feedback rather than global worker counts.
confidence: General principle only; not species-specific calibration
methods: Review covering several genera; publisher abstract/reference list inspected; full article not available in retrieval.
simplification: Age, crop deficit and individual response thresholds are modelling hypotheses, not fitted L. niger age schedules.

observation: Queen reserves support founding and adult workers emerge over weeks.
mechanism: Claustral provisioning, worker-mediated care after emergence.
confidence: High for husbandry observations, low for our exact stage durations
methods: 286 collected queens, 23°C climate chamber; untreated founding cohort separate from manipulated CRISPR eggs.
measurements: First walking workers at 42 days after collection; 137 colonies established on days 42–52; last at day 87. 56% established. These are colony-first-event observations, not individual stage distributions.
implementation: Simulation.physiology/updateBrood/layEgg; queen reserve pools; DAY units
simplification: 17/14/21-day stages and reserves are assumptions. CRISPR injection mortality is deliberately not transferred to normal eggs.

observation: Thermal development responses vary among populations; low temperatures can induce larval diapause.
methods: University author repository abstract inspected; publisher full text unavailable. Indexed table excerpts not used as calibration.
measurements: Repository describes 17–20°C versus 22–27°C responses; no fitted coefficients imported.
simplification: Cold halt is reversible numerical approximation; seasons, true diapause and population adaptation absent.

observation: Workers remove conspecific corpses; response depends on time since death.
mechanism: Local corpse cues, without globally dispatched cleaners.
confidence: High for necrophoresis; cue kinetics approximate
methods: Twelve laboratory nests; batches of five freeze-killed nestmates placed inside nest; observed transport outside.
measurements: Fresh-corpse trials: 15% moved at 1 h, 28.3% at 3 h, all by 54 h. This does not support a universal 2 h hard threshold.
simplification: 2 h deterministic cue delay and wandering disposal are provisional; no specific chemical asserted, no disease model.

observation: Richer sucrose sources elicited more marking; trail influence decays.
mechanism: Quality-modulated deposited marks with exponential persistence.
confidence: High for laboratory measurements; surface-dependent calibration
methods: Beckers, Deneubourg & Goss 1993, Journal of Insect Behavior 6:751–759. Ten 2000–3000-worker colonies; six decay trials; Y-bridge choices.
measurements: 1 M versus 0.05/0.1 M: 43% more marks. Exponential mean lifetime 47 min, SE 9.5 min; this is NOT half-life. Converted half-life = 47×60×ln(2) seconds.
simplification: Relative signal units, saturating response and uniform substrate. Default decay is a laboratory estimate, not universal field persistence.

observation: Surface temperature affects excavation depth and chamber placement.
mechanism: Environmentally responsive nest modification; proximate individual rules unresolved.
confidence: Dataset metadata inspected, raw data restricted
methods: Garcia Ibarra et al. dataset; associated paper DOI 10.1111/1365-2656.14040. Soil-column scans on days 7/14/28/88; 17 young colonies, 100-day study described in PubMed abstract.
measurements: Dataset lists excavation masses, temperatures, 3D morphology and workers. Raw ODS files are access-restricted; no distributions imported.
implementation: Depth metric and temperature sensitivity hooks; no empirical morphology fit
validation: G; external comparison pending authorized data access
simplification: No invented depth targets; 2D output cannot directly match 3D void volumes.
